log.point: Chloe, who knows 'some JavaScript', is given the hardest Python work in the plan: server-side image checks, decoded-dimension limits, resizing and re-saving, metadata stripping, a 500 KB cap and storage quota checks, all in Django/Pillow, in 7 hours. On top of that, her week-two testing covers full storage and interrupted uploads.
log.reason: Simplified photo processing to standard Pillow operations, budgeted two pairing hours for both Ana and Chloe, and removed automatic quotas and full-storage/interrupted-upload tests.

log.point: Ana has basic Python and no Django experience, but she gets 12 hours to set up Django and build accounts with reset, recipe and comment saving, ownership checks and admin removal. No time is set aside to learn Django. The ownership checks exist only because the plan assumes members can edit their posts, which the brief never asks for.
log.reason: Removed member editing, deleting and ownership checks, added a day-one Django tutorial hour, and kept Ana within 18 planned hours.

log.point: The plan wants email-and-password login but never says how. Django's default user logs in with a username. Switching to email login needs a custom user model or an email-auth backend, and the custom user model has to exist before the first migration.
log.reason: Ana creates and configures the custom email user model before the first migration and records that requirement in the shared instructions.

log.point: The audience is 60 classmates and their families, but the hosting step is an open-ended 2-hour check with no candidate host. It also sets a 2 GB storage bar that free hosts rarely meet, so the plan in practice slides to a laptop-only demo that the families can never use.
log.reason: Named PythonAnywhere for the day-one trial, replaced the 2 GB requirement with an allowance based on actual available space, and kept the laptop only as a failed-hosting fallback.
